q: Li and Yorke's theorem 'Period Three Implies Chaos' states that if a continuous map f: ℝ→ℝ has a period-3 point, then:
opts: f has infinitely many periodic points of every period
f has a period-3 point and possibly others
f is conjugate to the doubling map
The topological entropy is exactly log 3
exp: Li–Yorke (1975): if f has a period-3 point, then for every n≥1 f has a period-n point. Moreover there is an uncountable scrambled set of points with chaotic (Li–Yorke) behaviour. Sharkovskiy's theorem gives the full picture.
